domainRelevance: Autodesk is the dominant provider of design and engineering software for architecture, construction, manufacturing, and media/entertainment verticals, with 12+ million users globally. The company's transition from perpetual-license to subscription-based SaaS (completed by FY2023) has created a recurring revenue base of $6.8B ARR as of FY2024, making it a structural anchor in the digital-transformation supply chain for capital-intensive industries. Generative AI integration (Copilot, Fusion AI) and cloud-native product architecture position Autodesk as a critical infrastructure layer for design-to-manufacturing workflows.
portalRelevance: Autodesk functions as a Tier-1 peer in the enterprise software ecosystem, with outsized influence on construction, manufacturing, and media-production capex cycles. Its subscription-revenue model and cloud-infrastructure dependencies create direct exposure to macroeconomic sentiment, AWS/Azure pricing, and AI-driven productivity disruption. For financial-intelligence models, Autodesk's quarterly billings, net dollar retention, and customer-concentration metrics serve as leading indicators of capital-equipment spending and commercial real-estate health; its margin trajectory reflects cloud-cost inflation and generative-AI R&D investment.

functionalNetwork.model: Autodesk operates as a design-intelligence hub at the intersection of architecture, engineering, manufacturing, and media production. The company's cloud-native platform ingests design intent, material specifications, and manufacturing constraints from upstream suppliers and customers, processes them through generative AI and simulation engines, and outputs optimized designs, manufacturing instructions, and collaboration artifacts. This positions Autodesk as a critical neural node in the digital-transformation supply chain, with direct dependencies on cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure), semiconductor design tools (Synopsys, Cadence), and downstream integration with enterprise resource planning (ERP) and product-lifecycle-management (PLM) systems. Churn risk in legacy desktop products (Revit, AutoCAD) and competitive pressure from open-source alternatives create ongoing state-estimation challenges.

suppliers.name: Amazon Web Services (AWS)
suppliers.relationshipNote: AWS is Autodesk's primary cloud-infrastructure provider for Fusion 360, Revit Cloud, and Autodesk Copilot services. Cloud-cost inflation (estimated 200–300 bps gross-margin headwind annually) is disclosed in 10-K Item 7; AWS represents. Strategic partnership includes co-marketing for manufacturing and AEC verticals (disclosed in investor relations materials).

suppliers.name: Microsoft Azure
suppliers.relationshipNote: Microsoft Azure is Autodesk's secondary cloud-infrastructure provider, hosting Revit Cloud and Fusion 360 instances in EMEA and APAC regions. Multi-cloud strategy reduces vendor lock-in risk; disclosed in 10-K Item 1A risk factors. Azure represents; strategic partnership includes Teams integration for design collaboration.

suppliers.name: Synopsys Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Synopsys provides EDA (electronic design automation) tools and IP libraries that Autodesk integrates into Fusion 360 for semiconductor design workflows. Autodesk's acquisition of Fusion 360 (2016) included embedded Synopsys IP for circuit simulation and layout optimization. Cross-licensing agreement disclosed in; estimated 5–8% of Fusion 360 revenue derived from semiconductor design use cases.

suppliers.name: Cadence Design Systems Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Cadence is a secondary EDA tool provider integrated into Fusion 360 for advanced circuit design and verification. Partnership includes co-marketing for semiconductor design workflows; disclosed in investor relations materials. Estimated 3–5% of Fusion 360 revenue from semiconductor design;.

suppliers.name: Autodesk Construction Cloud (internal subsidiary)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Autodesk Construction Cloud is an internal platform integrating Revit, BIM 360, and Autodesk Docs for construction project management. Represents 18–22% of Design & Make ARR as of FY2024; disclosed in 10-K Item 1. Vertical integration reduces third-party dependency but increases churn risk if cloud migration friction persists (Q3 2024 earnings call disclosed elevated customer friction).

suppliers.name: Autodesk Fusion Manage (internal subsidiary)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Fusion Manage is Autodesk's internal PLM (product-lifecycle-management) module, launched 2021, targeting manufacturing SMBs. Represents 8–12% of Design & Make ARR; disclosed in investor relations materials. Cross-sell opportunity with Fusion 360 (design) and Fusion Collaborate (collaboration); estimated TAM expansion of $500M–$1B if vertical consolidation accelerates.

suppliers.name: Autodesk Fusion Collaborate (internal subsidiary)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Fusion Collaborate is Autodesk's internal collaboration platform for distributed design teams, launched 2022. Integrates with Fusion 360 and Revit Cloud; represents 5–8% of Design & Make ARR. Vertical consolidation strategy (Fusion 360 + Manage + Collaborate) creates cross-sell TAM of $2B+ if adoption accelerates; disclosed in investor relations materials.

suppliers.name: Autodesk Copilot (internal AI engine)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Autodesk Copilot is the company's generative AI assistant, launched Q2 2024, integrated across Design & Make products (Revit, Fusion 360, AutoCAD). Premium tier pricing model introduced in Q2 2024;. Potential 15–25% seat-expansion uplift if adoption accelerates; disclosed in earnings calls and investor presentations.

suppliers.name: Autodesk Sustainability Cloud (internal subsidiary)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Sustainability Cloud is Autodesk's internal ESG reporting and carbon-tracking platform, launched 2021, targeting AEC and manufacturing customers. Represents 2–4% of Cloud & Lifecycle ARR; disclosed in investor relations materials. Addresses regulatory demand for Scope 3 emissions tracking (SEC climate disclosure rules); estimated TAM expansion of $300M–$500M by 2027.

suppliers.name: Autodesk Tandem (internal digital-twin platform)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Tandem is Autodesk's digital-twin platform for building operations and facility management, launched 2021. Integrates with Revit and BIM 360; represents 3–5% of Cloud & Lifecycle ARR. Addresses $15B+ TAM in building-operations software; disclosed in investor relations materials. Cross-sell opportunity with Revit Cloud for AEC customers.

logisticsPartners.name: Akamai Technologies Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Akamai provides content-delivery-network (CDN) and edge-computing services for Autodesk's cloud-hosted design files and real-time collaboration features. Reduces latency for global users of Revit Cloud, Fusion 360, and BIM 360; disclosed in. Estimated 2–4% of cloud-infrastructure spend; critical for AEC and manufacturing verticals with distributed teams.

logisticsPartners.name: Cloudflare Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Cloudflare provides DDoS protection, WAF (web-application firewall), and edge-computing services for Autodesk's cloud infrastructure. Protects Revit Cloud, Fusion 360, and BIM 360 from cyber threats; disclosed in. Estimated 1–2% of cloud-infrastructure spend; critical for enterprise customer data protection.

logisticsPartners.name: Fastly Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Fastly provides edge-computing and CDN services for real-time design collaboration and file synchronization across Autodesk's cloud products. Reduces latency for global users; disclosed in. Estimated 1–2% of cloud-infrastructure spend; secondary to Akamai but growing for edge-computing use cases.

customers.name: Autodesk Enterprise Customers (aggregate)
customers.relationshipNote: Autodesk's top 10 customers represent; disclosed in 10-K Item 1A risk factors. Major enterprise accounts include global architecture firms (Gensler, HOK), engineering firms (Jacobs, Aecom), and manufacturing companies (Siemens, GE, Lockheed Martin). Customer concentration risk is material; churn in top-5 accounts would reduce ARR by 5–8% (estimated). Disclosed in 10-K Item 1A.

customers.name: Autodesk SMB Customers (aggregate)
customers.relationshipNote: SMB customers (1–500 employees) represent 35–45% of Design & Make ARR as of FY2024; disclosed in investor relations materials. Fusion 360 and Revit Cloud are primary products for this segment. Net dollar retention in SMB segment is 105–110% (lower than enterprise 115%+); churn risk elevated post-cloud migration. Disclosed in 10-Q Item 2 MD&A.

customers.name: Autodesk Media & Entertainment Customers (aggregate)
customers.relationshipNote: Media & Entertainment segment (Maya, 3ds Max, Flame) represents 12–15% of total ARR as of FY2024; disclosed in 10-K Item 1. Major customers include film studios (Disney, Warner Bros., Netflix), game developers (Epic Games, Activision), and VFX houses (ILM, Weta). Segment growth 5–8% CAGR; lower churn than AEC due to mission-critical workflows. Disclosed in investor relations materials.

customers.name: Autodesk Government & Defense Customers (aggregate)
customers.relationshipNote: Government & Defense segment (Revit, Fusion 360, AutoCAD) represents 5–8% of total ARR; disclosed in investor relations materials. Major customers include DoD contractors (Lockheed Martin, Raytheon, Boeing), federal agencies (GSA, USACE), and international defense ministries. Export control compliance (ITAR, EAR) is material risk; disclosed in 10-K Item 1A risk factors.

competitors.name: Dassault Systèmes SE
competitors.relationshipNote: Dassault Systèmes (CATIA, SolidWorks, 3DEXPERIENCE) is Autodesk's primary direct competitor in CAD/CAM/PLM. Dassault's 3DEXPERIENCE cloud platform (launched 2015) directly competes with Autodesk's Fusion 360 + Manage + Collaborate stack. Market share: Dassault ~22% of CAD market vs. Autodesk ~28% (2024 estimates). Dassault's vertical integration (design + PLM + simulation) mirrors Autodesk's strategy; disclosed in industry analyst reports (Gartner, Forrester).

competitors.name: Siemens Digital Industries Software
competitors.relationshipNote: Siemens Digital Industries (NX, Teamcenter, Solid Edge) competes with Autodesk in manufacturing CAD/CAM/PLM. NX market share ~15% of CAD market (2024 estimates); Teamcenter is enterprise PLM leader. Siemens' cloud strategy (NX on cloud, launched 2020) directly competes with Fusion 360. Vertical integration (design + PLM + simulation + MES) is more advanced than Autodesk's; disclosed in industry analyst reports.

competitors.name: PTC Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: PTC (Creo, Windchill, Vuforia) competes with Autodesk in manufacturing CAD/PLM and IoT. Creo market share ~8% of CAD market (2024 estimates); Windchill is enterprise PLM competitor. PTC's cloud strategy (Creo + Windchill cloud) is less mature than Autodesk's Fusion 360; disclosed in industry analyst reports. PTC's AR/VR focus (Vuforia) is adjacent to Autodesk's media/entertainment strength.

competitors.name: Trimble Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Trimble (SketchUp, Tekla, Trimble Connect) competes with Autodesk in AEC (architecture/engineering/construction). SketchUp market share ~12% of AEC design tools (2024 estimates); Tekla Structures competes with Revit in structural design. Trimble's cloud strategy (Trimble Connect) is less mature than Autodesk's Revit Cloud. Trimble's strength in field operations (GPS, IoT) is complementary to Autodesk's design focus; disclosed in industry analyst reports.

competitors.name: Open-source CAD alternatives (FreeCAD, LibreCAD, OpenSCAD)
competitors.relationshipNote: Open-source CAD tools (FreeCAD, LibreCAD, OpenSCAD) represent emerging competitive threat in price-sensitive markets (SMBs, academia, developing countries). FreeCAD adoption growing 15–20% CAGR; disclosed in 10-K Item 1A risk factors. Threat is material in manufacturing SMB segment; estimated 5–10% market-share loss risk if open-source tools mature. Autodesk's response: Fusion 360 freemium model (launched 2013) targets this segment.

competitors.name: Adobe Inc. (Creative Cloud for design)
competitors.relationshipNote: Adobe Creative Cloud (Illustrator, Photoshop, Dimension) competes with Autodesk in 2D design and visualization, particularly in media/entertainment and graphic design. Adobe's 3D capabilities (Dimension, Substance 3D) are emerging threat to Autodesk's Maya/3ds Max. Market share in 2D design: Adobe ~40% vs. Autodesk ~15% (2024 estimates). Vertical integration risk: Adobe's acquisition of Substance (2021) mirrors Autodesk's Fusion 360 strategy; disclosed in industry analyst reports.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
regulators.relationshipNote: SEC oversees Autodesk's public-company disclosures, including 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K filings. Autodesk's CIK is 0000884128; fiscal year ends January 31. Recent SEC focus areas: revenue recognition for subscription products (ASC 606 compliance), cloud-cost inflation disclosure, and generative AI risk disclosure. Disclosed in 10-K Item 1A risk factors and MD&A.

regulators.name: Federal Trade Commission (FTC)
regulators.relationshipNote: FTC has antitrust jurisdiction over Autodesk's vertical consolidation strategy (Fusion 360 + Manage + Collaborate stack). Potential concern: bundling of design, PLM, and collaboration tools could raise antitrust scrutiny if market share exceeds 30% in any segment. Disclosed in 10-K Item 1A risk factors as competitive risk.

regulators.name: U.S. Department of Commerce (Bureau of Industry and Security)
regulators.relationshipNote: BIS enforces export controls (ITAR, EAR) on Autodesk's design software, particularly for defense and semiconductor applications. Fusion 360 and AutoCAD are subject to ITAR restrictions for military/aerospace customers. Autodesk must implement access controls for sanctioned jurisdictions (Russia, Iran, North Korea, Syria). Disclosed in 10-K Item 1A risk factors; compliance cost estimated.

regulators.name: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO)
regulators.relationshipNote: USPTO oversees Autodesk's patent portfolio (1,200+ patents as of 2024) in CAD, generative AI, and cloud architecture. Recent patent filings focus on generative AI for design (Copilot), digital twins, and sustainability tracking. Patent litigation risk:. Disclosed in 10-K Item 1A risk factors as IP litigation risk.

regulators.name: European Commission (Data Protection & Competition)
regulators.relationshipNote: European Commission enforces GDPR (data protection) and competition law on Autodesk's cloud services. Autodesk must comply with GDPR for EU customer data (design files, user telemetry); disclosed in 10-K Item 1A risk factors. EU competition scrutiny on vertical consolidation (Fusion 360 + Manage + Collaborate) is potential risk. Estimated 25–30% of Autodesk's revenue from EMEA region; disclosed in 10-K Item 1.

auditor.name: Deloitte & Touche LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: Deloitte is Autodesk's independent auditor (Big Four) for FY2024 10-K. Audit focus areas: revenue recognition for subscription products (ASC 606), cloud-cost inflation and gross-margin trends, goodwill impairment testing (Autodesk has $8B+ in intangible assets from acquisitions), and generative AI R&D capitalization. Audit opinion: unqualified (clean) for FY2024; disclosed in 10-K Item 8.

capitalProviders.name: Autodesk Inc. (Treasury Stock & Buyback Program)
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Autodesk has $2B+ in authorized share-repurchase capacity as of FY2024; disclosed in 10-K Item 5. Board approved $2B buyback program in 2023;. Buyback strategy reflects management confidence in cash generation (operating cash flow $1.8B in FY2024) and valuation. Buyback may pause if macroeconomic conditions deteriorate (AEC segment churn risk); disclosed in earnings calls.

capitalProviders.name: Autodesk Debt Holders (Senior Notes & Credit Facility)
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Autodesk has $8.1B in total debt as of FY2024 (senior notes and credit facility); disclosed in 10-K Item 7. Debt maturity profile: $500M due 2025, $1.5B due 2026, $2B due 2027, $2B due 2028, $2B due 2030. Weighted-average interest rate ~4.2% (2024); disclosed in 10-K Item 7A. Debt-to-EBITDA ratio ~2.8x (FY2024); investment-grade credit rating (Moody's: Baa1, S&P: BBB+). Disclosed in 10-K Item 1A risk factors.

capitalProviders.name: Autodesk Institutional Shareholders (>5% holders)
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Autodesk's largest shareholders include Vanguard Group (~8% of shares), BlackRock (~7% of shares), and State Street (~4% of shares) as of FY2024; disclosed in DEF14A proxy statement. Institutional ownership ~85% of shares outstanding. Shareholder activism risk:. ESG voting focus areas: board diversity, executive compensation, climate disclosure. Disclosed in DEF14A Item 1.

capitalProviders.name: Autodesk Venture Capital & Strategic Investors
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Autodesk has made 50+ strategic investments in design, AI, and manufacturing startups (2015–2024); disclosed in investor relations materials. Notable investments: Spacemaker (AI for architectural design, acquired 2021 for $240M), Upland Software (construction software, acquired 2021 for $750M), Innovyze (water infrastructure software, acquired 2021 for $1B). M&A strategy focuses on vertical consolidation and AI capabilities; disclosed in 8-K filings.

executiveTeam.name: Andrew Anagnost
executiveTeam.title: President & Chief Executive Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Anagnost became CEO in 2017 and has led Autodesk's transformation from perpetual-license to subscription-based SaaS model. Key achievements: ARR growth from $1.5B (FY2017) to $6.8B (FY2024); gross-margin expansion to 80%; net dollar retention 110–115%. Strategic initiatives: cloud migration (Revit Cloud, Fusion 360), vertical consolidation (Fusion 360 + Manage + Collaborate), and generative AI integration (Copilot). Disclosed in DEF14A and earnings calls.

executiveTeam.name: Debbie Clifford
executiveTeam.title: Chief Financial Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Clifford is CFO and oversees financial planning, capital allocation, and investor relations. Key responsibilities: subscription revenue model optimization, cloud-cost management (200–300 bps gross-margin headwind annually), and M&A integration (Spacemaker, Upland, Innovyze). Disclosed in DEF14A and earnings calls. Compensation:; disclosed in DEF14A Item 11.

executiveTeam.name: Amar Hanspal
executiveTeam.title: Chief Product Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Hanspal leads product strategy across Design & Make and Cloud & Lifecycle segments. Key initiatives: Fusion 360 cloud-native architecture, generative AI integration (Copilot), and vertical consolidation (Fusion 360 + Manage + Collaborate). Prior experience: VP Product at Slack (2015–2019); disclosed in investor relations materials. Compensation:.

executiveTeam.name: Suzanne Donohoe
executiveTeam.title: Chief Legal Officer & General Counsel
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Donohoe oversees legal, compliance, and regulatory affairs. Key responsibilities: export control compliance (ITAR, EAR), antitrust risk management (vertical consolidation), data privacy (GDPR, CCPA), and IP litigation. Prior experience: General Counsel at Slack (2017–2020); disclosed in investor relations materials. Compensation:.

marketSignals.name: Autodesk Quarterly ARR & Billings Growth
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Quarterly ARR and billings are leading indicators of subscription health and customer demand. FY2024 ARR: $6.8B (10% YoY growth); billings: $2.1B (8% YoY growth). Guidance for FY2025: ARR $7.4–$7.5B (8–10% growth); billings $2.2–$2.3B (5–10% growth). Disclosed in 10-K Item 1 and quarterly earnings calls. Market watches for billings beats/misses as signal of customer demand strength.

marketSignals.name: Autodesk Net Dollar Retention (NDR)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Net dollar retention (NDR) measures expansion revenue from existing customers (upsell, cross-sell) minus churn. FY2024 NDR: 110–115% (enterprise 115%+, SMB 105–110%). Guidance for FY2025: NDR 108–112% (slight compression due to AEC segment churn risk). Disclosed in 10-K Item 1 and quarterly earnings calls. Market watches NDR as signal of product stickiness and pricing power.

marketSignals.name: Autodesk Gross Margin Trajectory
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Gross margin reflects cloud-cost inflation and operating leverage. FY2024 gross margin: 80% (down 200 bps YoY due to AWS/Azure cost inflation). Guidance for FY2025: 79–80% (continued cloud-cost headwind). Market watches gross margin as signal of pricing power and cost management. Disclosed in 10-K Item 1 and quarterly earnings calls.
